newsitem.title: USA: Oct US stock fund cash flow revised to $13.47 bln.
newsitem.headline: Oct US stock fund cash flow revised to $13.47 bln.

text.p: The Investment Company Institute, a mutual fund industry group, revised its estimate for new cash flows into U.S. stock mutual funds to $13.47 billion in October, up from a preliminary estimate of $13 billion.
The figure compared with new cash flows in September of $17.37 billion, revised from a previous estimate of $17.4 billion, the group said.
Year-to-date net new cash flow into stock funds was $192.62 billion, compared with $97.51 billion through October 1995.

Although net new cash flow to stock mutual funds declined in October when compared with September, the combination of higher stock prices and inflows lifted assets of stock funds by 1.9 percent to $1.65 trillion, the group said.

Bond and income funds had an outflow of $383.4 million in October, revised from an outflow of $500 million. In September, there was an inflow of $1.91 billion, revised from an inflow of $1.93 billion.
Money market funds had an inflow of $21.41 billion in October, compared with an outflow of $12.15 billion in September. Money market flows typically fluctuate.

Net new cash flow is defined as the dollar value of new sales, less redemptions, combined with net exchanges. Exchanges are the value of funds a shareholder switches into or out of funds in the same complex.
